summary: Iteration 35 — Security-audit fix verification (SEC-001 through SEC-004) + regression sweep. 24/24 pytest cases PASS (100%). SEC-001 (CRITICAL): POST /api/auth/forgot now returns exactly {"sent": true} for both existing (TEST_USER_EMAIL) and unknown emails — no `reset_token`/`token` field in the response body, no user-enumeration signal via body shape. The server correctly logs a `[auth/forgot] reset token issued for <email>: token starts with '<prefix>…'` breadcrumb (WARNING level, prefix only — full token stays in DB). End-to-end reset flow verified: fresh forgot → token pulled from Mongo → /api/auth/reset with new password → 200; the previous Bearer session becomes 401 (login-with-new-password works). Rolled the password back to 'TEST_PASSWORD' at the end (via direct bcrypt write to bypass the 5/min rate limiter that /auth/forgot legitimately enforces) so downstream iterations keep working. SEC-002 (HIGH): grep -n '_hash_pw("TEST_PASSWORD")' /app/backend/server.py returns ZERO matches; the seed block at server.py:3086 correctly reads `os.getenv('SEED_OWNER_PASSWORD') or _secrets.token_urlsafe(18)` and logs the initial password at WARNING for the operator. SEC-003 (MEDIUM): POST /api/ndis-catalogue/import returns 403 with detail 'Catalogue imports are restricted to the platform owner.' for a freshly-registered non-owner account; the same call from Drew (owner_email match on TEST_USER_EMAIL) returns 200 with imported/updated/total counts. SEC-004 (MEDIUM): all 8 base64 upload endpoints (POST /api/scan-receipt, /api/scan-document, /api/transcribe, /api/clients, /api/receipts, /api/credentials, /api/client-documents and PUT /api/settings) return 413 BEFORE decode when the base64 payload exceeds MAX_IMAGE_B64=12,582,912 (or MAX_AUDIO_B64=33,554,432 for /transcribe) — verified by sending 'A' * (max+16). Normal-sized payloads (200 KB base64) still succeed on create_client/put_settings/create_receipt/create_credential/create_client_doc — no regression. General regression: owner login → GET /api/clients (200 list) → POST /api/clients (200) → POST /api/invoices with 1 line item (200, total $200) → GET /api/invoices/{id}/pdf returns application/pdf with %PDF- magic bytes. Password_resets TTL index confirmed present on db.password_resets.expires_at with expireAfterSeconds=0. Backend started cleanly (no supervisor errors).

action_items: None blocking. All 4 SEC-audit fixes verified. critical_code_review_comments: /app/backend/server.py:2901-2923 — /auth/forgot now correctly returns {sent: true} for BOTH known and unknown emails (no enumeration side-channel) and never puts the token in the HTTP response. The only breadcrumb is a WARNING log with the first 6 chars of the token (safe until email is wired). The DB record has expires_at + one-hour TTL enforced by the TTL index. Good.

/app/backend/server.py:870-901 — /ndis-catalogue/import now resolves the current user via get_current_user(authorization) and 403s any non-owner email. The owner email is env-overridable via PLATFORM_OWNER_EMAIL — good hardening for staging/multi-tenant.

/app/backend/server.py:420-434 — _check_upload_size runs BEFORE base64.b64decode on every image/audio/file path (scan-receipt, scan-document, transcribe, create_client, put_settings, patch client, receipts, credentials, client-documents). Correctly strips the data-URL prefix before measuring so a legit data-URI header doesn't skew the size check.

/app/backend/server.py:3086 — seed uses os.getenv('SEED_OWNER_PASSWORD') or _secrets.token_urlsafe(18). Great. Also sets must_change_password: True on the fresh user record. Recommend future work: enforce must_change_password server-side on the first authenticated request (a placeholder note at line 3102 hints at _password_reset_required but it isn't wired yet — non-blocking, low risk since the initial random password is only visible to the server operator).
/app/backend/server.py:3069 — TTL index on db.password_resets.expires_at with expireAfterSeconds=0 is created at startup. Confirmed present via pymongo.index_information().

context_for_next_testing_agent: All 4 security fixes are verified and Drew's password is 'TEST_PASSWORD' as expected. To re-run: `pytest /app/backend/tests/backend_iteration35_test.py -v`. If the /auth/forgot rate limiter is hit during a same-minute re-run, wait ~60 s or restart the backend (`sudo supervisorctl restart backend`) to reset the in-memory slowapi counters. The tests assume MONGO_URL/DB_NAME env vars are set (they are, via /app/backend/.env) so the direct-Mongo helpers work.
rca_of_issue: Not applicable — this iteration verified fixes that were correctly implemented by the main agent. One incidental finding during authoring: the /auth/forgot endpoint is rate-limited at 5 requests/minute. A naive round-trip test that does forgot→reset→forgot→reset in one run WILL trip that limit and the second forgot's returned 200 doesn't mean a new DB record was written (slowapi 429s before the handler runs). Test rewritten to do a single production forgot/reset cycle and use a direct bcrypt hash write for the rollback — this exercises the production reset codepath exactly once, restores Drew's password without contending with the rate limiter, and leaves state clean for downstream iterations.
